TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- 73% of U.S. adults have an unfavorable view of China, a 26-point rise since 2018 and a 7-point increase since March 2020, primarily due to perceived mishandling of the COVID-19 pandemic (Page 4)

- 77% of Americans have little or no confidence in President Xi Jinping (Page 5)

- 73% believe the U.S. should promote human rights in China even if it harms economic relations (Page 5)
- 52% of Americans view the U.S. as the world's leading economy, compared to 32% who hold this view for China, with a 7 percentage point decline in U.S. economic superiority over four months (Page 6)
- Republicans are significantly more likely than Democrats to have very unfavorable views of China and support tougher policies (Page 7)
- 73% of Americans have an unfavorable view of China, the highest level in 15 years, with 42% holding a very unfavorable view (Page 8)
- 83% of Republicans/Lean Reps have an unfavorable view of China compared to 68% of Democrats/Lean Dems (Page 8)
- Older Americans (ages 50 and older) are substantially more negative toward China (81%) than those ages 30 to 49 (71%) or those under 30 (56%), with a 10 percentage point increase since March among the 50+ group (Page 9)
- Republicans have consistently held more unfavorable views than Democrats, with the gap widening in recent months; 83% of Republicans and 68% of Democrats had an unfavorable opinion of China in 2020 (Page 10)
- 64% of Americans say China has done a bad job dealing with the coronavirus outbreak, with 43% rating it as a very bad job; 82% of Republicans and 73% of those aged 50+ find fault in China's response (Page 11)
- 51% of Americans say China's initial handling contributed a great deal to the virus's spread, with 73% of Republicans holding this view compared to 38% of Democrats (Page 12)
- 50% of Americans think the U.S. should hold China responsible for its role in the pandemic even if it means worsening economic relations, while 38% prioritize strong U.S.-China relations (Page 13)
- 68% of Americans view U.S.-China economic ties as bad, up from 53% in 2019, with increases of 15 points among Republicans and 12 points among Democrats (Page 14)
- 46% of Americans favor getting tougher with China economically, up 11 percentage points from the previous year, with 62% of Republicans supporting a tougher stance (Page 15)
- 73% of Americans believe the U.S. should prioritize promoting human rights in China over maintaining economic relations, with 78% of Democrats and 70% of Republicans supporting this view (Page 16)
- 57% of Americans see China as a competitor, down from 66% in 2012; 26% see China as an enemy, up from 15% in 2012 (Page 17)
- 52% of Americans still see the U.S. as the world's leading economic power, down from 59% in March 2020, while 32% see China as the top economy (Page 18)
- Democrats' views on the U.S. being the leading global economy dropped from 54% in March to 44% in June-July 2020, while Republican views remained stable (Page 19)
- 77% of Americans have not too much confidence or no confidence at all in President Xi Jinping, with 55% having no confidence at all (Page 20)
